dct_description_sm: Data was acquired in Dease Strait, near the community of Cambridge Bay, Nunavut, in order to examine small-scale surface topography changes over a three-week period in May.  An area of untouched slightly deformed snow-covered sea ice was used to measure a time-series of surface topography, while transects of ice and snow thickness were completed opportunistically outside of the non-invasive site.  The objective of this project was to examine how the surface topography of slightly deformed ice, and associated snow and ice thicknesses changed throughout the month of May in Dease Strait.  The LiDAR topographic surface measurements were acquired as a complementary dataset to the snow and ice thickness transect dataset.
dct_title_s: LiDAR Topographic Surface Measurements in Dease Strait: 2014
